answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost.
